It is ultimately likely that Bittle will be fine, provided that he recovers fully. The Raptors have little urgency to rush him, as he is much more of a long-term investment. 

They have signaled their commitment to him by giving him a two-way, which is probably the best he could do at this writing.

However, there are cautionary tales, particularly with big men. The worst case I could find was Brook Lopez, who had a series of fractures that cost him 100 games early in his career. 

Lopez has enjoyed a fine career, and the Raptors would be thrilled if Bittle followed in his footsteps.

An avulsion can mean many things, and there's not much to go on here as the Raptors have provided little information. Based on Bittle being in a walking boot, it's a fair guess that he has a stress fracture in his foot caused by a tendon/ligament pulling on a bone (perhaps most likely his baby toe).
